claim: Corporation income taxes peaked at 39.8 percent of all federal receipts in fiscal 1943 and stood at 35.4 percent in 1945 — roughly two of every five dollars Washington collected. By 2003 the corporate share was 7.4 percent, and it has stayed under 10 percent since; individual income and payroll taxes now carry most of the federal bill. The figures are the Office of Management and Budget's own historical tables. A line of dialogue in the 2000 video game Deus Ex — 'in 1945 corporations paid 50% of federal taxes, now they pay about 5%' — rounds both ends outward, but the collapse it describes is on the government's books.

notes: From capture Da_gguclVXo (Deus Ex NSF-terrorist dialogue reel). Verified against OMB Table 2.2 via govinfo (FY2005 edition): 1943 corporate 39.8%/individual 27.1%; 1945 corporate 35.4%/individual 40.7%; 2003 corporate 7.4%/individual 44.5%. Recent years ~6-10% (2020: 6.2%). On an income-taxes-only basis the game's '50%' is closer: 1943 corporate was 59% of combined income-tax receipts. Game quote transcribed from the capture audio.
